title: How AI coding rewired Matt Pocock's brain: tests, deep modules, and friction
summary: Matt Pocock lists nine shifts after months of fully AI-written code. He now invests in integration tests, strong feedback loops (types, hooks, CI), deep grey-box modules, aggressive UI prototyping, and just-in-time docs, while managing the extra cognitive load of keeping up with agent changes.

principles.text: Raise test boundaries to integration/e2e level so AI agents can run code and you catch more bugs.
principles.quote: Raising test boundaries lets you catch more bugs and work more comfortably with AI agents running code automatically.

principles.text: Run pre-commit hooks, CI and type checking on every AI change; immediate feedback gives agents real-world context.
principles.quote: Every single change the AI makes should trigger your pre-commit hooks, CI, and type checking so bugs get caught immediately.

principles.text: Prototype UI aggressively: ask for several options on throwaway routes before committing to a PRD.
principles.quote: Ask the LLM for five different options for the UI change. Put them on throwaway routes so you can look at them.

principles.text: Prefer a few deep modules with simple interfaces over many shallow modules with big interfaces.
principles.quote: Bad codebases have lots of shallow modules with big interfaces. Good codebases have a few big modules with simple interfaces.

principles.text: Treat deep modules as grey boxes: test at the boundaries and leave the implementation to the AI.
principles.quote: Break your codebase into large modules and test at the boundaries. Then leave the implementation to the AI.

principles.text: Avoid stuffing repos with markdown docs; they rot and confuse LLMs. Let the AI generate docs just in time.
principles.quote: Let the AI generate its own docs during the exploration phase instead. Those docs never go out of date because they're just-in-time generated.
